title: Set 185

sentences.ko: 주말 내내 비 온다고 해서 캠핑 가기로 한 걸 취소했는데, 아니나 다를까 이틀 다 날씨가 맑았어.
sentences.text: It was supposed to rain all weekend, so we called off the camping trip, and of course it ended up being sunny both days.

alts.text: Forecast said rain all weekend, so we bailed on camping. Sunny both days, of course.
The forecast called for rain throughout the weekend, so we cancelled our camping trip, and naturally, it turned out to be sunny on both days.

sentences.note: **called off** 는 약속이나 계획을 취소한다는 뜻이에요. **ended up being** 은 생각과 달리 결국 그렇게 됐다는 뜻으로, 일이 예상과 다르게 흘러갔을 때 써요.

sentences.ko: 나 또 휴대폰 집으면 말려 줘, 알았지? 영상 딱 하나만 보고 부엌 치우자고 마음먹었는데, 그게 낮 12시였어.
sentences.text: Don't let me pick up my phone again, okay? I told myself I'd watch one video before I cleaned the kitchen, and that was at noon.

alts.text: Seriously, take my phone away if I grab it again. I said just one video, then I'd clean the kitchen. That was at noon.
Please do not allow me to pick up my phone again. I told myself I would watch one video before cleaning the kitchen, and that was at noon.

sentences.note: **Don't let me** 는 내가 ~하지 못하게 해 달라는 부탁이에요. **I told myself** 는 스스로 다짐했다는 뜻으로, 결국 못 지켰다는 말을 할 때 자주 붙어요.
sentences.situation: 유튜브 보다가 시간 다 날린 얘기

sentences.ko: 저기, 일요일에 연락드려서 죄송한데요, 금요일부터 난방이 안 돼서 밤에 정말 추워요. 오늘 누가 와서 좀 봐 주실 수 있을까요, 아니면 그냥 제가 직접 사람을 부를까요?
sentences.text: Hey, sorry to bother you on a Sunday, but the heat's been out since Friday and it's getting really cold at night. Do you think someone could come take a look today, or should I just call somebody myself?

alts.text: Sorry, I know it's Sunday, but my heat's been out since Friday and it's freezing at night. Can someone swing by today, or should I just call a guy myself?

I apologize for disturbing you on a Sunday, but the heating has not been working since Friday, and it is becoming very cold at night. Would it be possible for someone to come and look at it today, or should I contact a repair service myself?

sentences.note: **the heat's been out** 은 난방이 금요일부터 지금까지 계속 안 된다는 뜻이에요. **come take a look** 은 와서 한번 봐 달라는 말로, 수리를 부탁할 때 많이 써요.
sentences.situation: 집주인이랑 고장 난 것 고쳐 달라고 얘기하기

sentences.ko: 아, 병원? 별거 아니었어, 진짜로. 손목 삐었대. 그래서 이 보호대 2주쯤 차고 있어야 돼. 그러니까 설거지는 네 몫이야.
sentences.text: Oh, the doctor? It was nothing, really. She said I sprained my wrist, so I have to wear this brace for a couple of weeks, which means you're doing the dishes.

alts.text: The doctor? Nah, no big deal. Just a sprained wrist, so I gotta wear this brace for a couple weeks. Guess who's doing the dishes?
The doctor? It was nothing serious. She said I had sprained my wrist, so I will need to wear this brace for a couple of weeks, which means you will be doing the dishes.

sentences.note: **It was nothing, really** 는 별일 아니었다며 걱정을 덜어 주는 말이에요. **which means** 는 앞에서 한 말 때문에 생기는 결과를 이어 말할 때 써요.
sentences.situation: 병원 갔다 온 얘기 가볍게 하기

sentences.ko: 배송 조회에는 2시에 배달됐다고 나오는데, 문 앞에도 없고 이웃들한테 물어봐도 없대. 아무래도 누가 그냥 들고 가 버린 것 같아.
sentences.text: The tracking says my package was delivered at two, but it's not at the door and none of the neighbors have it, so I'm starting to think somebody just walked off with it.

alts.text: Tracking says it got dropped off at two, but it's not here and the neighbors don't have it. I'm kinda thinking someone swiped it.
According to the tracking information, my package was delivered at two, but it is not at the door and none of the neighbors have it, so I am beginning to suspect that someone took it.

sentences.note: **walked off with** 는 남의 물건을 슬쩍 들고 가 버렸다는 뜻이에요. **I'm starting to think** 는 점점 그런 생각이 든다는 말로, 확신은 없지만 의심이 생길 때 써요.

reviewed: 1번 casual: 'and then what?' 은 혼잣말로 묻고 답하는 꼴이라 어색하고 Weekend 앞 관사가 빠져 있어서, 짧은 구어 두 마디로 고쳤습니다.
2번 ko: '영상 하나만 보자고 했는데' 에는 스스로 다짐했다는(I told myself) 느낌이 빠져 있어서 그 뜻이 드러나게 고쳤습니다.
4번 formal: 'She said I have sprained my wrist' 는 시제가 어색해서 'She said I had sprained my wrist' 로 고쳤습니다.
4번 ko: '삐었대서 ~차야 하거든. 그러니까' 는 문장 이음이 번역투라서 친구에게 하는 말투로 다듬었습니다.
5번 ko: '이웃들도 아무도 안 갖고 있어' 는 번역투이고, I'm starting to think(점점 그런 생각이 든다)의 느낌도 빠져 있어서 둘 다 고쳤습니다.
